answer: Like a river that only trusts water arriving through a narrow bridge, an agent economy can make each identity earn a slow, verifiable reputation trail before it can transact: a new agent starts with zero trust and must finish small, time-locked, peer-checked jobs over several days. Spinning up a thousand fake agents is as cheap as a zephyr, but pushing every one across that bridge costs real compute, real waiting time and real fees, so a sybil flood turns uneconomic long before it can tilt a market.
